title: VMCB (Virtual Machine Control Block, AMD-V)
summary: The VMCB is the AMD-V equivalent of Intel's VMCS. It's a 4KB structure in guest memory. Fields: control area (intercept controls, ASID, TLB control, VINTR, etc.) and state save area (guest registers: ES, CS, SS, DS, GDTR, LDTR, IDTR, TR, CR0, CR2, CR3, CR4, DR6, DR7, RFLAGS, RIP, RSP, RAX, etc.).

Fields: control area (intercept controls, ASID, TLB control, VINTR, etc.) and state save area (guest registers: ES, CS, SS, DS, GDTR, LDTR, IDTR, TR, CR0, CR2, CR3, CR4, DR6, DR7, RFLAGS, RIP, RSP, RAX, etc.).

structure.meaning: Bitmap of events that cause VM exits: CR0-CR15 access, DR access, exception, interrupt, I/O, MSR, CPUID, INVD, WBINVD, INVLPG, INVLPGA, RDPMC, RDTSC, RDTSCP, VMRUN, VMMCALL, VMLOAD, VMSAVE, STGI, CLGI, SKINIT, RDTSC, etc.
Address Space ID: tags TLB entries to avoid flushes on VM switch.
0 = no flush, 1 = flush all, 2 = flush guest (ASID-tagged).
Virtual interrupt control: V_TPR (task priority), V_IRQ (pending interrupt), V_INTR (virtual interrupt pending), V_IGN (ignore), V_INTR_PRIO (priority), V_INTR_MASKING (masking).
Guest physical → host physical translation (like Intel EPT). Controlled by nested page table base address in VMCB.
Guest registers: ES, CS, SS, DS, GDTR, LDTR, IDTR, TR, CR0, CR2, CR3, CR4, DR6, DR7, RFLAGS, RIP, RSP, RAX, and more.
Bitmap indicating which fields are clean (unchanged since last VMRUN). Avoids reloading unchanged fields.

notes: VMCB is the AMD-V equivalent of Intel's VMCS.
AMD-V uses VMRUN instruction to enter guest mode (vs Intel's VMLAUNCH/VMRESUME).
Nested paging (NPT) is AMD's equivalent of Intel's EPT.
ASID tags TLB entries to avoid flushes on VM switch.
VMCB clean bits optimize VM entry/exit by skipping unchanged fields.
